text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak banking sector on Tursday, for the second time this year, did not meet the NBS minimum reserves requirement but dealers said this was caused by a mistake in calculation of the reserves.

- The European Union expects Slovakia to cancel by June 5, 1997, an import deposit measure which requires importers to deposit 20 percent of the value of imported goods on an interest-free account for 180 days.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Thursday met his Dutch counterpart Wim Kok to discuss Slovakia's integration to western structures. Meciar said he believed the meeting with Kok helped Slovakia to get closer to the EU.
- The Constitutional Court said on Thursday it had so far not ruled on the motion of whether the constitution can be changed by a referendum.
- Production of Slovakia's largest pharmaceutical company, Slovakofarma a.s., rose to 4.97 billion crowns in 1996, from 4.34 billion in 1995.
- Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft said it planned to build six new petrol stations in the Czech Republic this year to incerase the overal number of its Czech units to 33.
PRAVDA - The Slovak state-owned gas distributor SPP said the planned joint-venture with Russian gas producer Gazprom will only deal with supplies of gas above the already contracted amounts.
- SPP said Gazprom will take 40 percent of its profit from the joint-venture with SPP through deliveries of Slovak goods for its 400,000 employees.
- A visa-free agreement between Slovakia and Israel becomes effective by the middle of July 1997.
- European Commission representative to Bratislava, Sven Kuhn von Burgsdoff, on Thursday criticised the Slovak import deposit measure.
SME - European Union Foreign Relation Commissioner Hans van den Broek is expected to visit Slovakia on May 29 to discuss Slovak integration in the EU.
- Jan Carnogusrsky, leader of the strongest opposition party the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), said Slovakia's chances to start negotiations on EU membership will last only until May 29.

- President Michal Kovac said public Slovak Television twice barred him from presenting his contribution to the campaign on the NATO referendum in which he wanted to appeal for a "yes" vote in the plebiscite.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Arms production is expected to account for about 30 percent of the overall Slovak industrial production, up from the current 10 percent.
